title: Supply Chain and Artifact Evidence Baseline
concrete_capability_transition: Brownie release engineering gains a repository-local supply-chain and artifact evidence generator plus guard that records lockfile, dependency/security/license scan, secret scan, SBOM, checksum, provenance, artifact, smoke-test, and signing evidence slots while failing closed instead of treating missing evidence as Release Ready.

strategic_capability_mapping.transition: The local release gate now produces and validates bounded supply-chain and artifact evidence slots for the tested commit.
strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: This advances runtime-release-guard-ci by turning missing SBOM, checksum, provenance, artifact, scan, and signing evidence into explicit machine-checked release blockers rather than prose-only follow-up.

answers.strategic_capabilities: The phase advances headless_autonomous_development by making supply-chain and release-artifact evidence mechanically visible to the Runtime release gate.
answers.new_capability: A contributor can run pnpm --workspace-root release:supply-chain-artifact-evidence and guard:supply-chain-artifact-evidence to generate and validate bounded local evidence for lockfiles, dependency scan status, secret scan status, SBOM, checksums, provenance, artifacts, smoke tests, and signing/integrity status.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: The existing release contract named missing artifacts, SBOM, checksums, provenance, and scans but did not generate a concrete evidence file or validate satisfied evidence paths and hashes.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie could keep passing the local mandatory gate while still relying on manual interpretation of missing supply-chain evidence, making Release Ready drift harder to detect.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase does not repeat clippy, protocol, ledger, durable migration, or platform work; it adds the supply-chain and artifact evidence surface that those gates did not produce.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. No JSON-RPC method or Runtime protocol surface is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The generated evidence is a release artifact candidate for guards, not a new user-facing report or Runtime diagnostic endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Build/release behavior changes: pnpm release:gate now includes supply-chain evidence generation plus guard tests, and VSIX check invokes the contract-only guard path.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: The autonomous release loop can now distinguish missing release artifacts or scan tooling from successful Runtime behavior and continue closing concrete release evidence gaps.
answers.milestone_progress: RRP-8.4 narrows runtime-release-guard-ci from local mandatory quality gate success to explicit supply-chain and artifact evidence accounting while preserving runtime_release_ready=false.

non_goals: hosted services, scheduler, durable queue, supervisor, SaaS, RBAC, Vault, BDK, or Enterprise admin

reject_when: phase claims Runtime Release Ready or raises maturity to the target without artifact, scan, SBOM, checksum, provenance, review, and owner-setting evidence
missing artifacts, SBOM, checksum, signature or integrity proof, provenance, dependency audit, license audit, or secret scan evidence are treated as satisfied
generated release evidence stores raw prompt, provider response, file content, process output, absolute path, canonical path, environment value, executable content, credential, or secret material
workflow files are modified without workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent path
license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or signing infrastructure are changed by Runtime automation

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-8.4 changes release-gate and guard-engine files plus release-contract/audit manifests. Review must confirm supply-chain evidence generation is bounded, guards fail closed on missing or falsely satisfied evidence, release:gate invokes the generator and guard, VSIX check validates the contract-only guard path, no workflow file is edited without workflow scope, and runtime_release_ready remains false.

exit_criteria: pnpm --workspace-root release:supply-chain-artifact-evidence generates bounded local evidence with runtime_release_ready=false.

pnpm --workspace-root guard:supply-chain-artifact-evidence validates the release contract and generated evidence, rejecting missing sections, absolute paths, false Release Ready claims, and falsely satisfied evidence.
pnpm --workspace-root guard:supply-chain-artifact-evidence:test covers fail-closed negative cases.
pnpm release:gate includes supply-chain evidence generation and validation after the Release Contract guard.

runtime_release_ready remains false while actual release artifacts, smoke tests, audit tools, workflow provenance, signatures/integrity proof, owner settings, and independent reviews remain incomplete.
behavior_evidence: pnpm --workspace-root release:supply-chain-artifact-evidence generates .brownie/release-evidence/supply-chain-artifact-evidence.json with explicit fail_closed_reasons.
pnpm --workspace-root guard:supply-chain-artifact-evidence passes against generated evidence while keeping release_ready=false.
pnpm --workspace-root guard:release-contract and guard:release-contract:test require the new evidence contract and commands.
pnpm release:gate -- --evidence /tmp/brownie-rrp8-4-release-gate.json passes the repository-local mandatory gate while recording runtime_release_ready=false.
cargo test -p brownie-cli installed_run_timeout_retry_uses_same_admission_without_duplicate_task -- --exact --nocapture passes after warming first-touch runtime setup outside the timeout window.

accepted_capability: The repository-local release gate generates supply-chain and artifact evidence slots.
The supply-chain/artifact guard validates generated evidence and contract metadata.
Missing artifacts, scan tooling, smoke tests, workflow provenance, and signing or integrity authority remain explicit release blockers.
No Release Ready claim is made without complete evidence.
behavior_evidence: pnpm --workspace-root release:supply-chain-artifact-evidence generates .brownie/release-evidence/supply-chain-artifact-evidence.json with explicit fail_closed_reasons.
pnpm --workspace-root guard:supply-chain-artifact-evidence passes against generated evidence while keeping release_ready=false.
pnpm --workspace-root guard:release-contract and guard:release-contract:test require the new evidence contract and commands.
pnpm release:gate -- --evidence /tmp/brownie-rrp8-4-release-gate.json passes the repository-local mandatory gate while recording runtime_release_ready=false.
cargo test -p brownie-cli installed_run_timeout_retry_uses_same_admission_without_duplicate_task -- --exact --nocapture passes after warming first-touch runtime setup outside the timeout window.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains execution, admission, replay, permission, MCP, workspace mutation, durable state, protocol, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection clients and cannot grant Runtime authority.
GitHub workflow settings, branch protection, protected tags, signing authority, license choice, and publish posture remain owner-controlled until explicitly provided.
Raw prompt, provider output, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, and process output are not persisted as release evidence.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not edit .github workflow files without workflow scope.
Does not generate or publish release tags, packages, license metadata, signatures, or release assets.

Does not add hosted scheduler, daemon, durable queue, supervisor, SaaS control plane, customer RBAC, Vault, billing, BDK, Enterprise admin, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, or remote Git capability expansion.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected crate-level clippy allow because the mandatory gate should expose real warning debt.
Rejected marking runtime-release-guard-ci closed because workflow hardening, artifacts, scans, SBOM, checksums, provenance, reviews, and owner-controlled settings remain incomplete.
Rejected editing .github/workflows/ci.yml because the active credentials do not have workflow scope.
technical_debt: runtime-release-guard-ci remains open until actual vulnerability/license audits, cross-platform artifacts, artifact smoke tests, workflow enforcement, provenance, signing/integrity, branch protection/status checks, independent reviews, and owner settings are complete.
Owner license, publish posture, signing or integrity mechanism, branch protection, protected tags, and independent reviews remain required before Runtime Release Ready.
next_capability_rationale: Continue with supply-chain, artifact, cross-platform, soak, and governance release evidence that can be implemented locally, then return to workflow hardening when workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent path exists.

runtime_release_dod: Closed RRP-1 through RRP-7.2 and RRP-5.18 evidence remains in force and is not reimplemented.
RRP-8.2 establishes the Release Engineering Contract and local gate baseline while keeping runtime_release_ready false.
Missing release artifacts, scans, SBOM, checksums, signatures or integrity proof, provenance, workflow run, tested commit, and independent reviews remain release-blocking.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, durable queues, worker leases, hosted isolation, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside local Runtime v0.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside this phase.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging publication, license choice, signing authority, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain owner-controlled or later release work.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-8.2.

technical_debt.next_action: Add remaining repository-local artifact, supply-chain, cross-platform, soak, governance, and permitted CI evidence, then wire mandatory workflow once workflow scope or owner-approved equivalent path exists.
Owner must provide workflow-scope credentials or approve an equivalent CI-hardening path before direct .github workflow gate closure.
Owner must choose license and publish posture before public OSS release; Runtime automation must not change license, publish metadata, release tags, or release assets.

closeout_review.evidence: RRP-8.2 defines the release engineering contract and local gate baseline but does not claim artifact, security, cross-platform, governance, workflow, or owner-setting completion.
